content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"Most conclusions trace to cited evidence (testing consultant's confirmation of full time, selectee qualifications, rankings, Complainant's 64.4 score vs. cut-offs), but the protected-basis analysis is thin: the comparators (White and Hispanic candidates) are mentioned without any link to the finding of no animus, and the cut-off scores and score derivation are not stated."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations are attributed (Proctor, Chief DUSM, Assistant Chief, Branch Chief, testing consultant, Career Board Presenter), but some are unattributed or hearsay-like, such as the 'all candidates' pat-down claim, the claim that Complainant 'admitted' limited experience with no cited source, and the underlying assessment guidelines, which are not cited by document."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Key dates are present (Aug 31, 2017 test; Sept 11, 2017 meeting; Nov 2, 2017 selections; June 2019 decision, June 2021 reissue), but the dates of the complaint to HR, the retest denial, the EEO contact, and the prior pat-downs ('a week before') are vague or missing, and the period of the non-selection vacancies is not defined."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The record does not show who authored the final decision, what threshold governed the assessment cut-offs, or how Complainant's responses and rebuttals were weighed before finalization; the Career Board's process and the 11 vacancies where he did not make the certificate are not documented beyond the Branch Chief's testimony."},"rc5":{"status":"review","note":"The record is partly self-contained on the testing events and the two Best Qualified List selections, but gaps in cut-off scores, comparator treatment, reprisal-knowledge evidence and decision-maker identification mean an independent reviewer would need outside context to fully assess the conclusion."}}}
